summary: iter_12 focused on new PayPal Orders v2 integration (mock-fallback path since PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID/SECRET are empty). Wrote /app/backend/tests/test_v12_paypal_orders.py — 15 tests, 12 PASS / 3 FAIL. CRITICAL BUG FOUND: the mock-fallback path in POST /api/billing/paypal/create-order returns `order_id` in the JSON response but never persists that field to db.checkout_sessions. It only writes `session_id`. Then POST /api/billing/paypal/capture queries `db.checkout_sessions.find_one({order_id: req.order_id, user_id: ...})` and always returns 404 — the entire mock flow is broken end-to-end. Reproduced with a raw curl: create-order returned session_id='cs_paypal_139981844a834c9baafff3a9' + order_id='cs_paypal_139981844a834c9baafff3a9', immediate capture with that same value → 404 'PayPal order not found for this user'. The real-PayPal branch (line 231-244) correctly stores `order_id`; only the mock branch (line 197-211) forgot it. Fix is one line: add `"order_id": session_id` to the mock session dict before `db.checkout_sessions.insert_one(...)`. WHAT PASSES: /api/billing/paypal/status returns {configured:false, mode:null} correctly; create-order for pro returns mocked:true, provider:paypal, tier:pro, amount:29, approval_url:null, status:pending, order_id starts 'cs_paypal_'; studio path returns amount:99; free tier and unknown tier both correctly 400; auth-gate returns 401 on create-order & capture without bearer; capture with a genuinely unknown order_id returns 404 (correct — but this is only 'correct' because ALL mock orders look unknown due to the bug); regression on /api/integrations/connections (4 providers), /api/billing/checkout (Stripe cs_stripe_ + tier flip), /api/billing/upgrade all still green. MINOR OBSERVATION: /api/billing/paypal/status has no auth dependency in the code (billing.py:175) despite the review request stating 'auth required' — the endpoint currently returns 200 without a bearer token. Not security-sensitive (leaks nothing), but a contract mismatch. Frontend testing was intentionally skipped per the review request (mock flow already covered in iter_11 checkout-confirm test; real WebBrowser path not testable without live keys). No expo/react-native deprecated packages or SafeAreaView issues introduced by this iteration.

critical.issue: Mock-fallback branch in paypal_create_order (billing.py:197-211) stores only `session_id` in db.checkout_sessions but never `order_id`. The capture endpoint (billing.py:251-254) looks up by `order_id` → every mock capture returns 404 'PayPal order not found for this user'. Tier never flips. Feature is 100% broken in the mock path. One-line fix: add `"order_id": session_id,` to the mock session dict, matching the real-flow branch at line 233.

minor.issue: Review request states this endpoint requires auth, but billing.py:176 defines it without `Depends(current_user)`. Currently returns 200 to unauthenticated callers. Either add the dep or update the spec — no data leak either way (only exposes {configured, mode}).

integration_issues.issue: Because the create-order → capture backend flow is broken (see backend CRITICAL), the UI PayPal path in /app/frontend/app/pricing.tsx will get a 200 on create-order followed by a 404 on capture — user will see the error state (checkout-retry / checkout-cancel-error) instead of a tier flip. Not exercised by playwright this iteration (skipped per request) but will fail once fix is applied and retested.

critical_code_review_comments: billing.py:197-211 (BUG SOURCE) — mock-fallback branch writes `session_id` but not `order_id`; the response spreads `{**session, 'order_id': session_id}` so the API consumer sees `order_id`, but the DB doc has no `order_id` key. Capture (billing.py:252) filters by `order_id` → guaranteed 404. Classic 'response-vs-persistence divergence'. Fix by adding the field to the persisted doc, not just the returned dict.
billing.py:175-180 — `/paypal/status` handler has no `Depends(current_user)`. Everywhere else in this router uses it. Likely oversight. Doesn't leak data but breaks the auth-gate contract.

paypal_client.py:21-25 — Env is read at import time and cached in module-level constants (`PAYPAL_CLIENT_ID`, `_BASE`). Fine for prod but means adding keys later requires a backend restart — worth documenting.
paypal_client.py — Uses async httpx + PayPal-Request-Id for idempotency on both create and capture. Modern, correct approach. Good.
billing.py:187 — `if req.tier not in TIERS or TIERS[req.tier]['price_monthly'] == 0:` correctly rejects both 'free' and unknown tiers with a single 400 (matches spec).
billing.py:251-253 — capture lookup is user_id-scoped (prevents cross-user capture hijack). Good.
billing.py:261 — capture correctly branches on `session.get('mocked')` OR `not paypal_client.is_configured()` — defensive OR, handles the case where keys are added between create and capture. Good.
billing.py:290 — capture_id extraction wrapped in try/except (KeyError, IndexError) — sensible for PayPal's nested response shape.
No hardcoded URLs. httpx timeout set to 15-20s. Errors mapped to 502 with truncated messages — no PII leak.
paypal_client.py has no unit tests since PayPal keys aren't set — acceptable, but once keys are added the get_access_token cache + create_order path should be exercised with the sandbox.

rca_of_issue: Root cause: in /app/backend/billing.py, the `paypal_create_order` endpoint has two branches — real PayPal (when keys are set) and a mock fallback (when keys are empty). The real branch (lines 231-244) constructs a session_record with BOTH `session_id` AND `order_id` fields (both equal to the PayPal order id) and inserts it into db.checkout_sessions. The mock fallback branch (lines 197-208) constructs a session dict with only `session_id` — it forgets `order_id`. The response body then does `return {**session, 'order_id': session_id, 'approval_url': None}` which adds order_id to the RESPONSE but not the persisted document. Later, `paypal_capture` (line 251) does `db.checkout_sessions.find_one({'order_id': req.order_id, 'user_id': ...})` — since no mock document has an `order_id` field, this always returns None → 404. Reproduction: 1) POST /api/billing/paypal/create-order {tier:'pro', return_url:'x', cancel_url:'y'} with bearer 'audit-token' → note the returned order_id. 2) POST /api/billing/paypal/capture {order_id: <the value from step 1>} → 404 'PayPal order not found for this user'. Mitigation / fix: add `"order_id": session_id,` to the session dict at ~line 199 (or anywhere between session_id and mocked). One-line change. After fix, 3 currently-failing tests (test_paypal_capture_flips_tier_to_pro, test_paypal_capture_idempotent_second_call, test_paypal_capture_studio_order_flips_tier) will pass.
